title: Scene props
description: Repeated environmental objects — street trees, benches, lamps, bollards, planters — declared as instances of a small set of prototypes. Kept separate from the asset registry because props are high-count, low-information and usually decorative: a district has thousands of them, none carries a metadata panel, and most are grade C or D. Separating them keeps the registry meaningful and lets a viewer render them with GPU instancing. The viewer knows the prototype VOCABULARY, never the specific assets; a module supplies both the prototypes and the placements. See SCENE-DRESSING.md.

instances.description: Placements. Flat and compact on purpose: a district can have tens of thousands.

kind.description: Vocabulary the viewer understands. A viewer MAY substitute its own built-in geometry for a known kind when no payload is supplied, which is what lets a district look inhabited before any modelling work is done.

url.description: Payload for the prototype mesh. When absent, the viewer falls back to procedural geometry for the declared kind.

size_m.description: Nominal footprint and height, used by procedural fallbacks and for culling.

billboard.description: Render as a camera-facing quad rather than geometry. Appropriate for distant vegetation.

seasonal_foliage.description: What this prototype looks like through the year, as a colour per season. Present because a street tree is not one colour: a ginkgo is famously pure yellow for about ten days in November and a Callery pear is white in April, and rendering both mid-green all year is the main reason procedural vegetation reads as identical props rather than as trees. A viewer that ignores this simply renders the prototype's default appearance.

deciduous.description: True when the prototype loses its leaves. Distinct from the winter colour because it changes the GEOMETRY, not the tint: a bare tree is a crown of twigs, and drawing it as a solid mass in winter brown reads as a dead tree rather than a dormant one.

extensions.description: Module-private payloads, keyed by module_id. A viewer MUST ignore extensions it does not recognise.

instance.description: One placement. Deliberately terse: `p` is the prototype, `xy` the scene position, `r` an optional yaw in degrees, `s` an optional uniform scale.

z.description: Ground height. Omit to let the viewer snap to its terrain, which is usually what you want.

tile.description: Owning tile ID, so props can stream with the tile rather than all at once.
